PITA.extract: Pinus taeda, commonly known as loblolly pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native to the Southeastern United States, from East Texas to Florida, up to southern New Jersey. The wood industry classifies the species as a southern yellow pine. U.S. Forest Service surveys found that loblolly pine is the second-most common species of tree in the United States, after red maple. For its timber, the pine species is regarded as the most commercially important tree in the Southeastern U.S. The common name loblolly is given because the pine species is found mostly in lowlands and swampy areas.
PITA.commons_file: File:Moon Tree in Waycross, GA, US.jpg
PITA.photo_credit: Photo: Jud McCranie, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PSME.extract: The Douglas fir is a conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae. It is the tallest tree in the family. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine. There are three varieties: coast Douglas-fir, Rocky Mountain Douglas-fir and Mexican Douglas-fir.
PSME.photo_author: USDA-NRCS PLANTS Database / Herman, D.E. et al. 1996. North Dakota tree handbook. USDA NRCS ND State Soil Conservation Committee; NDSU Extension and Western Area Power Admin., Bismarck, ND.
PSME.photo_credit: Photo: USDA-NRCS PLANTS Database / Herman, D.E. et al. 1996. North Dakota tree handbook. USDA NRCS ND State Soil Conservation Committee; NDSU Extension and Western Area Power Admin., Bismarck, ND., Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

PIPO.description: Species of pine tree in western North America
PIPO.extract: Pinus ponderosa, commonly known as the ponderosa pine or western yellow pine, is a very large pine tree species of variable habitat native to mountainous regions of western North America. It is the most widely distributed pine species in North America.
PIPO.photo_credit: Photo: Walter Siegmund (talk), CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons

QUAL.extract: Quercus alba, the white oak, is one of the preeminent hardwoods of eastern and central North America. It is a long-lived oak, native to eastern and central North America and found from Minnesota, Ontario, Quebec, and southern Maine south as far as northern Florida and eastern Texas. Specimens have been documented to be over 450 years old.
QUAL.commons_file: File:Keeler Oak Tree - distance photo, May 2013.jpg
QUAL.photo_credit: Photo: Marty Aligata at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PIAL.description: Pine tree species found in North America
PIAL.extract: Pinus albicaulis, known by the common names whitebark pine, white bark pine, white pine, pitch pine, scrub pine, and creeping pine, is a conifer tree native to the mountains of the western United States and Canada, specifically subalpine areas of the Sierra Nevada, Cascade Range, Pacific Coast Ranges, Rocky Mountains, and Ruby Mountains. It shares the common name "creeping pine" with several other plants.
PIAL.commons_file: File:2013-09-16 16 04 07 Large Whitebark Pine at about 9550 feet along the Island Lake Trail in Lamoille Canyon, Nevada.jpg
PIAL.photo_credit: Photo: Famartin, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PIED.extract: Pinus edulis, the pinyon pine, Colorado pinyon, or simply pinyon, is a species of pinyon pine from the southwestern United States noted for its large, edible seeds. Although all of the species in its section of the pine genus are called pinyon pines this is the species most associated with the name.
PIED.photo_credit: Photo: jotor at Flickr, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

JUVI.extract: Juniperus virginiana, also known as eastern red cedar, red cedar, Virginian juniper, eastern juniper, red juniper, and other local names, is a species of juniper native to eastern North America from southeastern Canada to the Gulf of Mexico and east of the Great Plains. Farther west it is replaced by the closely related Juniperus scopulorum and to the southwest by Juniperus ashei. It is not to be confused with Thuja occidentalis.
JUVI.commons_file: File:2014-05-13 08 32 55 Eastern Red Cedar at South Riding Golf Club in South Riding, Virginia.JPG
JUVI.photo_credit: Photo: Famartin, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ARTR2.extract: Artemisia tridentata, commonly called big sagebrush, Great Basin sagebrush or simply sagebrush, is an aromatic shrub from the family Asteraceae.
ARTR2.commons_file: File:Artemisia tridentata ssp. vaseyana - mountain big sagebrush - Flickr - Matt Lavin (1).jpg
ARTR2.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
ARTR2.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

VAME.extract: Vaccinium membranaceum is a species of flowering plant in the heath family Ericaceae, known by the common names thinleaf huckleberry, tall huckleberry, big huckleberry, mountain huckleberry, square-twig blueberry, and "black huckleberry".
VAME.commons_file: File:Heidelbeere (Vaccinium membranaceum) im Nordamerika-Quartier des Forstbotanischen Gartens Tharandt (1).jpg
VAME.photo_credit: Photo: Aagnverglaser, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

VAAN.extract: Vaccinium angustifolium, commonly known as the wild lowbush blueberry and the low sweet berry is a species of blueberry native to eastern and central Canada, Great Lakes and the northeastern United States.
VAAN.photo_credit: Photo: Ayotte, Gilles, 1948-, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PAQU.extract: American ginseng known in Kanienʼkéha as Tekaren’tó:ken is a species of flowering plant in the ivy family Araliaceae. It is native to eastern North America although its cultivation was successfully introduced to China in 1975. The specific epithet quinquefolius means "five-leaved", which refers to the typical number of leaflets per leaf. It is one of a group of taxa known as "ginseng".
PAQU.photo_credit: Photo: Pittillo, Dan J., Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

EUES.extract: Euphorbia esula, commonly known as green spurge or leafy spurge, is a species of spurge native to central and southern Europe, and eastward through most of Asia north of the Himalaya to Korea and eastern Siberia. It can also be found in some parts of Alaska.
EUES.photo_author: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA
EUES.photo_credit: Photo: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CESO3.extract: Centaurea solstitialis, the yellow star-thistle, is a species of thorny plant in the genus Centaurea, which is part of the family Asteraceae. A winter annual, it is native to the Mediterranean Basin region and invasive in many other places. It is also known as golden starthistle, yellow cockspur and St. Barnaby's thistle.
CESO3.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BRTE.extract: Bromus tectorum, known as downy brome, drooping brome, or cheatgrass, is a winter annual grass native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and northern Africa, but has become invasive in many other areas. It now is present in most of Europe, southern Russia, Japan, South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, Iceland, Greenland, North America, and western Central Asia. In the eastern US, B. tectorum is common along roadsides and as a crop weed, but usually does not dominate an ecosystem. It has become a dominant species in the Intermountain West and parts of Canada, and displays especially invasive behavior in the sagebrush steppe ecosystems, where it has been listed as noxious weed. B. tectorum often enters the site in an area that has been disturbed, and then quickly expands into the surrounding area through its rapid growth and prolific seed production.
BRTE.photo_credit: Photo: Forest and Kim Starr, CC BY 3.0 us, via Wikimedia Commons

BOGR2.extract: Bouteloua gracilis, the blue grama, is a long-lived, warm-season (C4) perennial grass, native to North America.
BOGR2.photo_author: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA
BOGR2.photo_credit: Photo: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PSSP6.extract: Pseudoroegneria spicata is a species of perennial bunchgrass known by the common name bluebunch wheatgrass. It is native to western North America.
PSSP6.commons_file: File:Agropyron spicatum - bluebunch wheatgrass - Flickr - Matt Lavin.jpg
PSSP6.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
PSSP6.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ACRU.description: Maple tree native in North America
ACRU.extract: Acer rubrum, the red maple, also known as swamp maple, water maple, or soft maple, is a North American tree species. Many of its features, especially its deciduous leaves, are quite variable in form. At maturity, it often attains a height around 30 metres (100 ft). Its flowers, petioles, twigs, and seeds are all red to varying degrees.
ACRU.photo_credit: Photo: M.O. Stevens, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PRSE2.extract: Prunus serotina, commonly called black cherry, wild black cherry, rum cherry, or mountain black cherry, is a New World deciduous tree or shrub in the rose family, Rosaceae. Despite its common names, it is not very closely related to commonly cultivated cherries.
PRSE2.commons_file: File:Ruhland, Ortrander Str. 9d, Spätblühende Traubenkirsche auf dem Wohnhof Ortrander Str. 8-9, Frühling, 01.jpg
PRSE2.photo_credit: Photo: Wilhelm Zimmerling PAR, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

QURU.description: Species of flowering plant in the beech and oak family
QURU.extract: Quercus rubra, the northern red oak or common red oak, is an oak tree in the red oak group. It is a native of North America, in the eastern and central United States and southeast and south-central Canada. It has been introduced to small areas in Western Europe, where it can frequently be seen cultivated in gardens and parks. It prefers good soil that is slightly acidic. Often simply called red oak, northern red oak is so named to distinguish it from southern red oak (Q. falcata), also known as the Spanish oak.
QURU.commons_file: File:Red Oak Quercus rubra habit fall.jpg
QURU.photo_credit: Photo: Cossey25, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FRAM2.extract: Fraxinus americana, the white ash or American ash, is a deciduous tree in the olive family (Oleaceae) native to eastern and central North America. It is straight-trunked and fast-growing, reaching 60 to 90 feet tall with a canopy spread of 50 to 75 feet wide. The tree is highly valued as lumber for its straight grain and superior hardness.
FRAM2.commons_file: File:Fraxinus americana - University of Kentucky Arboretum - DSC09337.JPG
FRAM2.photo_credit: Photo: Daderot, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

LIST2.description: Species of tree in North America
LIST2.extract: Liquidambar styraciflua, commonly known as the American sweetgum among other names, is a deciduous tree in the genus Liquidambar native to warm temperate areas of eastern North America and tropical montane regions of Mexico and Central America. Sweetgum is one of the main valuable forest trees in the southeastern United States, and is a popular ornamental tree in temperate climates. It is recognizable by the combination of its five-pointed star-shaped leaves and its hard, spiked fruits. It is currently classified in the plant family Altingiaceae, but was formerly considered a member of the Hamamelidaceae.
LIST2.commons_file: File:Liquidambar styraciflua in Golden Valley Tree Park, May 2022 01.jpg
LIST2.photo_credit: Photo: Calistemon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ULAM.extract: Ulmus americana, generally known as the American elm or, less commonly, as the white elm or water elm, is a species of elm native to eastern North America. The trees can live for several hundred years. It is a very hardy species that can withstand low winter temperatures. The American elm was once exceptionally common as a street tree, its tolerance of urban conditions making it a popular choice to line American streets in the 19th and early 20th centuries. The coming of beetles bearing Dutch elm disease devastated the American elm population, starting in the 1920s. The species still holds out in some locations, but is also no longer nearly as common as during its height.
ULAM.commons_file: File:Elm Tree in Brattle Brook Park, Pittsfield, MA - August 2020.jpg
ULAM.photo_credit: Photo: Marty Aligata, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ACSA3.extract: Acer saccharum, the sugar maple, is a species of flowering plant in the soapberry and lychee family, Sapindaceae. It may also be called rock maple, sugar tree, sweet maple, or, particularly in reference to the wood, hard maple.
ACSA3.commons_file: File:Acer saccharum (sugar maple tree in fall colors) (Newark, Ohio, USA) (25 October 2024) 5.jpg
ACSA3.photo_credit: Photo: James St. John, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

NYSY.extract: Nyssa sylvatica, commonly known as tupelo, black tupelo, black gum or sour gum, is a medium-sized deciduous tree native to eastern North America from the coastal Northeastern United States and southern Ontario south to central Florida and eastern Texas, as well as Mexico.
NYSY.commons_file: File:2024-10-30 14 21 18 Black Tupelo changing color in autumn within Wells Mills Park in Ocean Township, Ocean County, New Jersey.jpg
NYSY.photo_credit: Photo: Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FRPE.extract: Fraxinus pennsylvanica, the green ash or red ash, is a species of ash native to eastern and central North America, from Nova Scotia west to southeastern Alberta and eastern Colorado, south to northern Florida, and southwest to Oklahoma and eastern Texas. It has spread and become naturalized in much of the western United States and also in Argentina and Europe, from Spain to Russia.
FRPE.photo_credit: Photo: Steven Katovich, USDA Forest Service, CC BY 3.0 us, via Wikimedia Commons

QUVE.extract: Quercus velutina, the black oak, is a species of oak in the red oak group, native and widespread in eastern and central North America. It is sometimes called the eastern black oak.
QUVE.commons_file: File:Brearley Oak, Lawrence Township, NJ - May 2013.jpg
QUVE.photo_credit: Photo: Msact, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

QUNI.extract: Quercus nigra, the water oak, is an oak in the red oak group, native to the eastern and south-central United States, found in all the coastal states from New Jersey to Texas, and inland as far as Oklahoma, Kentucky, and southern Missouri. It occurs in lowlands and up to 450 meters in elevation.
QUNI.commons_file: File:Black Oak Quercus nigra fall habit 04.jpg
QUNI.photo_credit: Photo: Cossey25, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

POTR5.description: Species of tree native North America
POTR5.extract: Populus tremuloides is a deciduous tree native to cooler areas of North America, one of several species referred to by the common name aspen. It is commonly called quaking aspen, trembling aspen, American aspen, mountain or golden aspen, trembling poplar, white poplar, and popple, as well as others. The trees have tall trunks, up to 25 metres tall, with smooth pale bark, scarred with black. The glossy green leaves, dull beneath, become golden to yellow, rarely red, in autumn. The species often propagates through its roots to form large clonal groves originating from a shared root system. These roots are not rhizomes, as new growth develops from adventitious buds on the parent root system.
POTR5.photo_credit: Photo: Famartin, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

OSVI.extract: Ostrya virginiana, the American hophornbeam, is a species of Ostrya native to eastern North America, from Nova Scotia west to southern Manitoba and eastern Wyoming, southeast to northern Florida and southwest to eastern Texas. Populations from Mexico and Central America are also regarded as the same species, although some authors prefer to separate them as a distinct species, Ostrya guatemalensis. Other names include eastern hophornbeam, hardhack, ironwood, and leverwood.
OSVI.photo_credit: Photo: Richard Webb, Bugwood.org, USA, CC BY 3.0 us, via Wikimedia Commons

JUOS.description: Western North American species of juniper
JUOS.extract: Juniperus osteosperma is a shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States.
JUOS.commons_file: File:2015-04-26 14 46 40 Old Utah Juniper on the summit of Grindstone Mountain, Nevada.jpg
JUOS.photo_credit: Photo: Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

QUMA2.extract: Quercus macrocarpa, the bur oak or burr oak, is a species of oak tree native to central and eastern North America. It is in the white oak section, Quercus sect. Quercus, and is also called mossycup oak, mossycup white oak, or scrub oak. The acorns are the largest of any North American oak, and are important food for wildlife.
QUMA2.photo_credit: Photo: Heath Cajandig, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

JUMO.extract: Juniperus monosperma, the New Mexico juniper or one-seed juniper, is a species of juniper native to western North America, in the United States in Arizona, New Mexico, southern Colorado, western Oklahoma (Panhandle), and western Texas, and in Mexico in the extreme north of Chihuahua. It grows at 970–2300 m elevation.
JUMO.photo_credit: Photo: Chris English, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PIMO.description: Pine tree found in North America
PIMO.extract: Pinus monophylla, the single-leaf pinyon, is a pine in the pinyon pine group, native to North America. The range is in southernmost Idaho, western Utah, Arizona, southwest New Mexico, Nevada, eastern and southern California and northern Baja California.
PIMO.photo_credit: Photo: Clinton Steeds at Flickr, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ABPR.extract: Abies procera, the noble fir, also called red fir, is a species of fir native to the Cascade Range and Pacific Coast Ranges of the northwestern Pacific Coast of the United States. It occurs at altitudes of 300–1,500 meters (980–4,920 ft).
ABPR.photo_credit: Photo: mamamusings on Flickr, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

LOJA.description: Flowering vine known as Japanese honeysuckle
LOJA.extract: Lonicera japonica, known as Japanese honeysuckle and golden-and-silver honeysuckle, is a species of honeysuckle native to East Asia, including many parts of China. It is often grown as an ornamental plant, but has become an invasive species in a number of countries. It is used in traditional Chinese medicine.
LOJA.photo_author: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA
LOJA.photo_credit: Photo: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

SYAL.extract: Symphoricarpos albus is a species of flowering plant in the honeysuckle family known by the common name common snowberry. Native to North America, it is browsed by some animals and planted for ornamental and ecological purposes, but is poisonous to humans.
SYAL.photo_credit: Photo: Iurie Nistor, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

MANE2.extract: Berberis nervosa, commonly known as dwarf Oregon-grape, Cascade barberry, Cascade Oregon-grape, or dull Oregon-grape, is a North American flowering plant.
MANE2.photo_credit: Photo: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

AMAL2.extract: Amelanchier alnifolia, the saskatoon berry, Pacific serviceberry, western serviceberry, western shadbush, or western juneberry, is a shrub native to North America. It is a member of the rose family, and bears an edible berry-like fruit.
AMAL2.photo_credit: Photo: Chris Light, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

SYOR2.extract: Symphoricarpos oreophilus is a North American species of flowering plant in the Caprifoliaceae, or honeysuckle family, known by the common name mountain snowberry.
SYOR2.photo_credit: Photo: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

VASC.extract: Vaccinium scoparium is a species of huckleberry known by the common names grouse whortleberry, grouseberry, and littleleaf huckleberry.
VASC.photo_author: Katja Schulz from Washington, D. C., USA
VASC.photo_credit: Photo: Katja Schulz from Washington, D. C., USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

HODI.extract: Holodiscus discolor, commonly known as ocean spray or oceanspray, creambush, ironwood, mountain spray, and rock-spiraea, is a shrub of western North America.
HODI.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
HODI.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PUTR2.extract: Purshia tridentata, with the common name bitterbrush, is a shrub in the genus Purshia of the family Rosaceae. It is native to mountainous areas of western North America.
PUTR2.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
PUTR2.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

GASH.extract: Gaultheria shallon is an evergreen shrub in the heather family (Ericaceae), native to western North America. Common names include salal, shallon, or gaultheria.
GASH.photo_credit: Photo: Chris Light, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

RUUR.extract: Rubus ursinus is a North American species of blackberry or dewberry, known by the common names California blackberry, California dewberry, Douglas berry, Pacific blackberry, Pacific dewberry and trailing blackberry.
RUUR.photo_credit: Photo: Walter Siegmund (talk), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ROMU.description: Species of flowering plant in the rose family
ROMU.extract: Rosa multiflora is a species of rose known commonly as multiflora rose, baby rose, Japanese rose, many-flowered rose, seven-sisters rose, Eijitsu rose and rambler rose. It is native to eastern Asia, in China, Japan, and Korea. It should not be confused with Rosa rugosa, which is also known as "Japanese rose", or with polyantha roses which are garden cultivars derived from hybrids of R. multiflora. It was introduced to North America, where it is an invasive species, forming extensive, impenetrable stands within forest understories, thickets, borders, and lowlands. It can be identified by its characteristic fringed stipules, which form pairs at the bases of leaf stalks bearing 3–89 leaves.
ROMU.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

VAPA.extract: Vaccinium parvifolium, the red huckleberry, is a species of Vaccinium native to western North America.
VAPA.photo_credit: Photo: Chris Light, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

SPBE2.extract: Spiraea betulifolia is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae. It is primarily native from Eastern Siberia to Korea and Northern and Central Japan. The historically recognized varieties native to North America are var. corymbosa, native to a portion of eastern North America, and var. lucida, now known as Spiraea lucida, native to British Columbia and the northwestern United States eastward to Sasketchewan and the Black Hills.
SPBE2.commons_file: File:Spirea betulifolia - Dunedin Botanic Garden - Dunedin, NZ - DSC04148.jpg
SPBE2.photo_credit: Photo: Daderot, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

RUPA.extract: Rubus parviflorus, the fruit of which is commonly called the thimbleberry, western thimbleberry or redcap, is a species of Rubus with large hairy leaves and no thorns.
RUPA.commons_file: File:Thimbleberry (Rubus parviflorus) - Unorganized North Algoma, Ontario 2024-06-22.jpg
RUPA.photo_credit: Photo: Ryan Hodnett, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

MARE11.description: Plant species in the buttercup family
MARE11.extract: Berberis repens commonly known as creeping mahonia, creeping grape holly, or creeping barberry, is a species of Berberis native to most of the western United States and two western provinces of Canada. It is low growing shrub that spreads by underground stems. As a species it is well adapted to fire and is a very common understory plant in western forests. An evergreen species, it provides food to deer and elk in winter and can make up a significant part of their diet. The berries are eaten by birds and small mammals, aiding it in spreading to recently disturbed areas. It has found use as a xeric ornamental plant and has escaped from cultivation in areas beyond its native range.
MARE11.photo_author: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA
MARE11.photo_credit: Photo: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CEMO2.extract: Cercocarpus montanus is a North American species of shrub or small tree in the family Rosaceae native to northern Mexico and the western United States. It is known by the common names alder-leaf mountain-mahogany, alder-leaf cercocarpus, and true mountain-mahogany. The variety argenteus is commonly known as silverleaf mountain-mahogany.
CEMO2.photo_credit: Photo: Chris Light, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CEVE.extract: Ceanothus velutinus, with the common names snowbrush ceanothus, red root, tobacco brush, and sticky laurel, is a species of shrub in the family Rhamnaceae. It is native to western North America from British Columbia to California to Colorado.
CEVE.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

JUCO6.description: Species of tree in the cypress family
JUCO6.extract: Juniperus communis, the common juniper, is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family Cupressaceae. An evergreen conifer, it has the largest geographical range of any woody plant, with a Holarctic distribution throughout the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere.
JUCO6.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

LATR2.extract: Larrea tridentata, also called creosote bush, greasewood as a plant, and chaparral as a medicinal herb. In Sonora, it is more commonly called hediondilla; Spanish hediondo = "smelly". It is a flowering plant in the family Zygophyllaceae. The specific name tridentata refers to its three-toothed leaves.
LATR2.commons_file: File:2014, A Large Creosote Bush, Mt. San Jacinto on the Horizon - panoramio.jpg
LATR2.photo_credit: Photo: Chris English, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

SYOC.extract: Symphoricarpos occidentalis, commonly called western snowberry, is a woody species of flowering plant in the honeysuckle family.
SYOC.photo_author: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA
SYOC.photo_credit: Photo: Andrey Zharkikh from Salt Lake City, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

KALA.extract: Kalmia latifolia, the mountain laurel, calico-bush, or spoonwood, is a flowering plant and one of the 10 species in the genus of Kalmia belonging to the heath(er) family Ericaceae. It is native to the eastern United States. Its range stretches from southern Maine to northern Florida, and west to Indiana and Louisiana. Mountain laurel is the state flower of Connecticut and Pennsylvania. It is the namesake of Laurel County in Kentucky, the city of Laurel, Mississippi, Mount Laurel, New Jersey, and the Laurel Highlands in southwestern Pennsylvania.
KALA.photo_credit: Photo: Basicdesign, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

SERE2.extract: Serenoa repens, commonly known as saw palmetto, is a small palm, growing to a maximum height around 200–300 cm (6.6–9.8 ft).
SERE2.photo_credit: Photo: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

LECU.extract: Lespedeza cuneata is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common names Chinese bushclover and sericea lespedeza, or just sericea. It is native to Asia and is present elsewhere as an introduced species and sometimes an invasive plant. Australian populations of Lespedeza juncea have sometimes been considered to belong to this species but are now considered to be distinct.
LECU.photo_credit: Photo: Dalgial, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

POMU.extract: Polystichum munitum, the western swordfern, is an evergreen perennial fern native to western North America, where it is one of the most abundant ferns in forested areas. It occurs along the Pacific coast from southeastern Alaska to southern California, and also inland east to southeastern British Columbia, northern Idaho and western Montana, with disjunctive populations in northern British Columbia, Canada; the Black Hills in South Dakota, United States; and Guadalupe Island off of Baja California, Mexico. Western swordfern is known to have locally naturalized in parts of Great Britain and Ireland.
POMU.photo_credit: Photo: Jami Dwyer, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ARCO9.extract: Arnica cordifolia is a species of arnica in the sunflower family, known by the common name heartleaf arnica. It is native to western North America.
ARCO9.photo_credit: Photo: Walter Siegmund (talk), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PTAQ.extract: Pteridium aquilinum, commonly called bracken, brake, pasture brake, common bracken, and also known as eagle fern, is a species of fern occurring in temperate and subtropical regions in both hemispheres. Originally native to Eurasia and North America, the extreme lightness of its spores has led to it achieving a cosmopolitan distribution. It is a herbaceous perennial plant with large, triangular fronds that grow from an underground rhizome.
PTAQ.photo_credit: Photo: Rasbak, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

LYJA.extract: Lygodium japonicum is a species of fern that is known by the common names Japanese climbing fern and vine-like fern. It is native to eastern Asia, from Pakistan through India east to Taiwan, Japan, Korea, and south through southeastern Asia to New Guinea. The fern is present in the southeastern United States, Puerto Rico, South Africa, and Australia as an introduced species.
LYJA.photo_credit: Photo: Kingfiser, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ACMI2.extract: Achillea millefolium, commonly known as yarrow or common yarrow, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. Growing to 1 metre tall, it is characterized by small whitish flowers, a tall stem of fernlike leaves, and a pungent odor.
ACMI2.commons_file: File:Yarrow (Achillea millefolium) in Longmire, though this plant is found widely in the park. (faf3f52c-7b81-4529-959e-887bc15b9609).JPG
ACMI2.photo_credit: Photo: NPS Photo, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

LIBO3.extract: Linnaea borealis is a species of flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae. It is the only species in the genus Linnaea. It is a boreal to subarctic woodland subshrub, commonly known as twinflower.
LIBO3.photo_credit: Photo: Brian Gratwicke from DC, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

XETE.extract: Xerophyllum tenax is a species of plants in the corn lily family. It is known by several common names, including bear grass, soap grass, quip-quip, and Indian basket grass. Beargrass can grow to be a little over 1.2 metres (4 ft) tall when in a preferred habitat and ideal conditions. The plant typically blooms at irregular intervals, depending on environmental factors such as moisture and temperature.
XETE.photo_credit: Photo: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FRVI.extract: Fragaria virginiana, known as Virginia strawberry, wild strawberry, common strawberry, or mountain strawberry, is a perennial North American strawberry that grows across much of the United States and southern Canada. It is one of the two species of wild strawberry that were hybridized to create the modern domesticated garden strawberry.
FRVI.photo_credit: Photo: Walter Siegmund (talk), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FRVE.extract: Fragaria vesca, commonly called the woodland strawberry, Alpine strawberry, wild strawberry, Carpathian strawberry or European strawberry, is a perennial herbaceous plant in the rose family that grows naturally throughout much of the Northern Hemisphere, and that produces edible fruits.
FRVE.photo_credit: Photo: James McNally, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

GUSA2.description: Plant species in the daisy family
GUSA2.extract: Gutierrezia sarothrae is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names broom snakeweed, broomweed, snakeweed, and matchweed. It is a subshrub native to much of the western half of North America, from western Canada to northern Mexico, and can be found in a number of arid, grassland, and mountain habitats. It can be toxic to livestock in large quantities, due mainly to the presence of saponins.
GUSA2.photo_credit: Photo: Alex Abair, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BASA3.extract: Balsamorhiza sagittata is a North American species of flowering plant in the tribe Heliantheae of the family Asteraceae known by the common name arrowleaf balsamroot. Also sometimes called Oregon sunflower or Okanagan Sunflower, it is widespread across western Canada and much of the western United States.
BASA3.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
BASA3.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ATFI.extract: Athyrium filix-femina, the lady fern or common lady-fern, is a large, feathery species of fern native to temperate Asia, Europe, North America, and North Africa. It is often abundant in damp, shady woodland environments and is often grown for decoration.
ATFI.photo_credit: Photo: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

THOC.extract: Thalictrum occidentale is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family known by the common name western meadow-rue. It is native to northwestern North America from Alaska and western Canada to northern California to Wyoming and Colorado, where it grows in shady habitat types such as forest understory and more open, moist habitat such as meadows.
THOC.photo_credit: Photo: Thayne Tuason, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ALPE4.description: Species of flowering plant in the cabbage family
ALPE4.extract: Alliaria petiolata, or garlic mustard, is a biennial flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae). It is native to Europe, western and central Asia, north-western Africa, Morocco, Iberia and the British Isles, north to northern Scandinavia, and east to northern Pakistan and Xinjiang in western China. It has now become a tenacious invasive plant across the northern U.S., in particular because of its earlier springtime emergence than many native species, often in the forest understory.
ALPE4.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CHAN9.extract: Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae. It is known in North America as fireweed and in the British Isles as both fireweed and rosebay willowherb. It is also known by the taxonomic synonyms Chamerion angustifolium and Epilobium angustifolium. It is native throughout the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including large parts of the boreal forests.
CHAN9.commons_file: File:P1000633 Epilobium angustifolium var. brachycarpum (Onagraceae) Plant.JPG
CHAN9.photo_credit: Photo: Magnus Manske, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CIAR4.extract: Cirsium arvense is a perennial species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native throughout Europe and western Asia, northern Africa and widely introduced elsewhere. The standard English name in its native area is creeping thistle. It is also commonly misnomered as Canada thistle and sometimes as field thistle.
CIAR4.photo_author: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA
CIAR4.photo_credit: Photo: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ARNU2.extract: Aralia nudicaulis is a species of flowering plant in the ivy family Araliaceae. It is native to northern and eastern North America.
ARNU2.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PUMO.extract: Pueraria montana, more commonly known as kudzu, is a species of plant in the botanical family Fabaceae. At least three sub-species are known. It is closely related to other species in the genus Pueraria and the common name is used for all of these species and hybrids between them. The morphological differences between them are subtle, they can breed with each other, and it appears that introduced kudzu populations in the United States have ancestry from more than one of the species.
PUMO.photo_credit: Photo: Bastique ☎ appelez-moi!, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ASSY.extract: Asclepias syriaca, commonly called common milkweed, butterfly flower, silkweed, silky swallow-wort, and Virginia silkweed, is a species of flowering plant. It is native to southern Canada and much of the United States east of the Rocky Mountains, excluding the drier parts of the prairies. It is in the genus Asclepias, the milkweeds. It grows in sandy soils as well as other kinds of soils in sunny areas.
ASSY.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ACRA7.extract: Actaea racemosa, the black cohosh, black bugbane, black snakeroot, rattle-top, or fairy candle, is a species of flowering plant of the family Ranunculaceae. It is native to eastern North America from the extreme south of Ontario to central Georgia, and west to Missouri and Arkansas. It grows in a variety of woodland habitats, and is often found in small woodland openings.
ACRA7.photo_credit: Photo: SB Johnny, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ALTR3.extract: Allium tricoccum is a bulbous perennial flowering plant in the amaryllis family Amaryllidaceae. It is a North American species of wild onion or garlic found in eastern North America. Many of the common English names for this plant are also used for other Allium species, particularly the similar Allium ursinum, which is native to Eurasia. An edible plant, Allium tricoccum is used in a variety of North American and indigenous cuisines, and has also been used by Native Americans in traditional medicine. A French rendering (chicagou) of a Miami–Illinois name for this plant is the namesake of the American city of Chicago.
ALTR3.photo_credit: Photo: Ayotte, Gilles, 1948-, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

MIVI.extract: Microstegium vimineum, commonly known as Japanese stiltgrass, packing grass, or Nepalese browntop, is an annual grass that is common in a wide variety of habitats and is well adapted to low light levels. It has become an invasive species throughout parts of the world, most notably North America.
MIVI.photo_author: James H. Miller & Ted Bodner, Southern Weed Science Society, Bugwood.org
MIVI.photo_credit: Photo: James H. Miller & Ted Bodner, Southern Weed Science Society, Bugwood.org, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CARU.extract: Calamagrostis rubescens is a species of grass known by the common name pinegrass.
CARU.photo_credit: Photo: Thayne Tuason, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CAGE2.extract: Carex geyeri is a species of sedge known by the common names Geyer's sedge and elk sedge. It is native to western North America from British Columbia to California to Colorado, where it grows in dry areas in mountain meadows, grasslands, and open forest. This sedge produces scattered tufts of stems connected by a network of long rhizomes. The stems are triangular in cross-section and approach half a meter in maximum height. The inflorescence is composed of a cluster of staminate flowers and a cluster of pistillate flowers separated by a node.
CAGE2.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
CAGE2.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FEID.extract: Festuca idahoensis is a species of grass known by the common names Idaho fescue and blue bunchgrass. It is native to western North America, where it is widespread and common. It can be found in many ecosystems, from shady forests to open plains grasslands.
FEID.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

POPR.extract: Poa pratensis, commonly known as Kentucky bluegrass, smooth meadow-grass, or common meadow-grass, is a perennial species of grass native to practically all of Europe, North Asia and the mountains of Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia. There is disagreement about its native status in North America, with some sources considering it native and others stating the Spanish Empire brought the seeds of Kentucky bluegrass to the New World in mixtures with other grasses. It is a very popular lawn grass in North America with the species being spread over all of the cool, humid parts of the United States. In its native range, Poa pratensis forms a valuable pasture plant, characteristic of well-drained, fertile soil. It is also used for making lawns in parks and gardens and has established itself as a common invasive weed across cool moist temperate climates like the Pacific Northwest and the Northeastern United States. When found on native grasslands in Canada, for example, it is considered an unwelcome exotic plant, and is indicative of a disturbed and degraded landscape.
POPR.photo_credit: Photo: Rasbak 08:35, 1 May 2007 (UTC), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

POSE.extract: Poa secunda is a widespread species of perennial bunchgrass native to North and South America. It is highly resistant to drought conditions, and provides excellent fodder; and has also been used in controlling soil erosion, and as revegetator, often after forest fires. Cultivars include 'Canbar', 'Service', 'Sherman', and 'Supernova'. Historically, indigenous Americans, such as the Gosiute of Utah, have used P. secunda for food. It was originally described botanically in 1830 by Jan Svatopluk Presl, from a holotype collected from Chile by Thaddäus Haenke in 1790.
POSE.commons_file: File:Artemesia tridentata var wyomingensis Wyoming big sagebrush and Poa secunda Sandberg bluegrass on Seedskadee National Wildlife Refuge (52087377309).jpg
POSE.photo_credit: Photo: USFWS Mountain Prairie, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

SCAR7.extract: Lolium arundinaceum, commonly known as tall fescue, is a cool-season, perennial C3 grass species native to Europe and introduced to North America and other parts of the world. It naturally occurs in grasslands and coastal marshes. Tall fescue is grown in a range of cultivars, widely used for livestock forage, in lawns and recreational areas as turf, and occasionally for managing soil erosion.
SCAR7.photo_author: Harry Rose from South West Rocks, Australia
SCAR7.photo_credit: Photo: Harry Rose from South West Rocks, Australia, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BOCU.extract: Bouteloua curtipendula, commonly known as sideoats grama, is a perennial, short prairie grass that is native throughout the temperate and tropical Western Hemisphere, from Canada south to Argentina.
BOCU.commons_file: File:Bouteloua racemosa - Botanical Garden, University of Frankfurt - DSC02534.JPG
BOCU.photo_credit: Photo: Daderot, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

ELEL5.extract: Elymus elymoides is a species of wild rye known by the common name squirreltail. This grass is native to central and western North America.
ELEL5.commons_file: File:Elymus elymoides squirrel-tail grass clump early-red.jpg
ELEL5.photo_credit: Photo: Dcrjsr, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CARO5.extract: Carex rossii, commonly known as Ross's sedge, is a hardy species of sedge that is often a pioneer species in areas with little or no established vegetation, or in places where disturbance has occurred. Ross's sedge grows in a variety of habitats throughout much of western North America, from Alaska to Ontario, south to New Mexico and California. It flowers in May and June.
CARO5.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ELGL.extract: Elymus glaucus is a species of grass known as blue wild rye or blue wildrye. This grass is native to North America from Alaska to New York to northern Mexico. It is a common and widespread species of wild rye.
ELGL.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
ELGL.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BRIN2.extract: Bromus inermis is a species of the true grass family (Poaceae). This rhizomatous grass is native to Europe and considered invasive in North America.
BRIN2.commons_file: File:Bromus inermis - smooth brome - Flickr - Matt Lavin (2).jpg
BRIN2.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
BRIN2.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

PHAR3.extract: Phalaris arundinacea, or reed canary grass, is a tall, perennial grass that commonly forms extensive single-species stands along the margins of lakes and streams and in wet open areas, with a wide distribution in Europe, Asia, northern Africa and North America. Other common names for the plant include gardener's-garters and ribbon grass in English, alpiste roseau in French, Rohrglanzgras in German, kusa-yoshi in Japanese, caniço-malhado in Portuguese, and hierba cinta and pasto cinto in Spanish.
PHAR3.photo_credit: Photo: Stefan.lefnaer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

FEAR2.extract: Festuca arizonica, commonly called Arizona fescue, is a grass found in western North America, in the southwest United States and northern Mexico. This species also has the common names mountain bunchgrass and pinegrass.
FEAR2.photo_author: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM
FEAR2.photo_credit: Photo: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

FEOC.extract: Festuca occidentalis is a species of grass known as western fescue. It is native to much of the northern half of North America and is most widely distributed in the west. It is most often found in forest and woodland habitat. The specific epithet occidentalis is Latin, meaning "western".
FEOC.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

MUMO.extract: Muhlenbergia montana, the mountain muhly, is a species of grass. It is native to North and Central America, where it is found throughout the Western United States, the Sierra Nevada, Mexico, and Guatemala.
MUMO.photo_author: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM
MUMO.photo_credit: Photo: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

BRVU.extract: Bromus vulgaris is a species of brome grass known by the common name Columbia brome.
BRVU.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
BRVU.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BRCA5.extract: Bromus carinatus is a species of brome grass known by the common names California brome and mountain brome.
BRCA5.photo_credit: Photo: Grzegorz Grzejszczak, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

BOER4.extract: Bouteloua eriopoda, commonly known as black grama, is a perennial prairie grass that is native to the Southwestern United States. Its main means of reproduction is by stolons, as its ratio of viable seeds to sterile ones is naturally low. The disparity may play a role in its lack of tolerance to overgrazing, but aside from this B. eriopoda is a good forage food for livestock.
BOER4.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
BOER4.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

CAPE6.extract: Carex pensylvanica is a species of flowering plant in the sedge family commonly called Pennsylvania sedge. Other common names include early sedge, common oak sedge, and yellow sedge.
CAPE6.photo_credit: Photo: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

TACA8.extract: Taeniatherum is a genus of Eurasian and North African plants in the grass family.
TACA8.photo_author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
TACA8.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

ANGE.extract: Andropogon gerardi, commonly known as big bluestem, is a species of tall grass native to much of the Great Plains and grassland regions of central and eastern North America. It is also known as tall bluestem, bluejoint, and turkeyfoot.
ANGE.photo_credit: Photo: Matt Lavin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
